column1: What is the degree of a vertex?
column2: The number of edges that touch it.

column1: When does a connected graph have an Euler circuit?
column2: Exactly when every vertex has even degree.

column1: When does a connected graph have an Euler path (not a circuit)?
column2: Exactly when it has two odd-degree vertices. The path starts at one and ends at the other.
Euler uses every edge once (easy to test). Hamilton visits every vertex once (NP-complete).

column1: What does \( (A^k)_{ij} \) count for an adjacency matrix \( A \)?
column2: The number of walks of length \( k \) from vertex \( i \) to vertex \( j \).

column1: What is a DAG and what does it guarantee?
column2: A directed graph with no directed cycle. It always has a topological order.

column1: How does Kahn's algorithm detect a cycle?
column2: It repeatedly removes vertices with no incoming arrows. Vertices left over at the end sit on or behind a cycle.
BFS finds fewest hops. Dijkstra finds lowest total weight when weights are non-negative.
